kurz: Salt does more than season. It draws out water, keeps water in meat, tightens bread dough and slows yeast.
bild_im_kopf: Like a tool with several blades: depending on timing and amount, it does something different.
was_passiert: On the surface, salt first draws water out. Given time, it penetrates, seasons all the way through and helps the meat hold its juice. In bread dough it strengthens the [[glutenbildung|gluten network]]; in large amounts it slows the yeast.
faustregeln: Salt meat right before cooking or many hours ahead, not 20–40 minutes before: then the drawn-out water sits on the surface.
Coarse salt for pre-salting, fine salt for seasoning.
Never put salt directly onto yeast.
